hypotheses.proposed_value: Multi-tiered SOC limits with dynamic adjustment based on thermal monitoring
hypotheses.mechanism_affected: Fraction of ejected heat during thermal runaway influenced by SOC and cell mass loss
hypotheses.causal_rationale: The failure was due to engineering infeasibility and regulatory incompatibility of a simple SOC cap. A dynamic system that adjusts SOC limits based on real-time thermal monitoring would address the causal mechanism (heat ejection influenced by SOC and mass loss) while being more feasible and potentially meeting regulatory requirements.
hypotheses.predicted_effect: Reduced thermal runaway propagation while maintaining higher average usable capacity
hypotheses.predicted_magnitude_or_range: 10-20% increase in usable capacity compared to fixed 75% limit
competing_explanations: Dynamic systems may introduce complexity and failure points
evidence_gaps: No evidence on regulatory acceptance of dynamic systems
no evidence on failure rates of such systems
hypotheses.falsifier: If the dynamic system shows equivalent or worse thermal runaway propagation compared to the fixed limit
hypotheses.measurement_required: Thermal runaway propagation testing with dynamic SOC limits under various conditions
